found: Menu page: 「オレンジバーベキューソースで仕上げました」 / 「ハニーマスタードソースで仕上げました」 / 「ピンク色のヨーグルトソースで仕立てました」 — with no allergen statement anywhere on the page.
method: 1 (mobile-host fetch of the Tabelog menu page)

quote: Savory chaffle sandwiches may use seasonings/soy-based sauces; wheat-content of these was not documented — ask before ordering.

note: Same evidence as the row above; cite the menu page. No source anywhere claims tamari or GF shoyu, so the 'ask' framing is correct rather than over-cautious.

quote: Egg and cheese are core to every chaffle; shared batter/griddle means egg and dairy are pervasive.
found: jp.japan-glutenfree.com: 「看板メニューのチャッフルは、欧米で糖質制限をしている人々の間で流行った人気料理で、チーズや卵などを使って作る低糖質ワッフルです。」 — and all five Tabelog menu items carry cheese and/or egg (スライスチーズ, カッテージチーズ, クリームチーズ, 目玉焼き, ゆで卵).
note: Fully evidenced and correct. A chaffle is by definition a cheese-and-egg batter.

quote: Brand is a dedicated gluten-free workshop (mincle) founded/led by a former nursery nutritionist, so allergy-awareness is central to the concept.
found: Tabelog PR: 「元保育園の栄養士が商品開発した素材にこだわったメニューの沢山あるカフェです。」; Instagram bio: 「元保育園栄養士のつくるワッフルサンドとスイーツのお店です byグルテンフリー工房mincle」; PR TIMES names 『グルテンフリー工房mincle』 and 「栄養士Natsumiを中心とした『食』のプロたち」.
note: The factual half — mincle brand, ex-nursery nutritionist doing product development — is evidenced. The inference 'so allergy-awareness is central to the concept' is NOT: every source frames mincle as 低糖質/ギルトフリー sweets; none describes an allergen protocol, staff training or celiac handling. Repair by citing the two facts and dropping the inference.

quote: Whole-shop wheat-free concept (no wheat flour used).
found: 「白砂糖、小麦粉を一切使用せず」 (Tabelog official 店舗PR).
note: True and citable. This is a takeout waffle shop with no wheat product on the menu, so it is a genuine whole-shop statement rather than a per-item one.

found: PR TIMES: 「グルテンフリー工房mincle監修の『グルテンフリーワッフルChaffle'ｓ（チャッフルズ）』のワッフルサンド」 and 「栄養士Natsumiを中心とした『食』のプロたち」.

note: Exact three-part match on the operator's own press release. The 添加物 element is absent from the Tabelog page, so cite PR TIMES (or the HAMONI listing) specifically.

quote: record-level assessment: gf_confidence=ask, vegan_status=limited, TRADING STATUS FAILS
found: Tabelog: 「このお店は店舗情報の確認が取れていないため掲載保留中です。」 (listing suspended as unconfirmed). Official Facebook page: 「突然ではありますが、Chaffle's浅草店を年内で閉店することとなり」. Japanese GF closed-shop register: 「グルテンフリーワッフル Chaffle's チャッフルズ／東京 … 閉店時期 2023年2月 … 場所 東京都文京区千石4-25-2」.
http: 200 (Tabelog mobile); 200 (closedshop register); Facebook body readable only via the Yahoo Japan verbatim snippet
method: 1 (mobile-host fetch) + 1 (plain fetch) + 4 (Yahoo Japan exact-string search on the Facebook announcement)
note: CLOSED, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The Asakusa branch announced its own closure on its official Facebook page and Tabelog has suspended the listing as unconfirmed. Worse, the record's gf_detail tells the reader 'the Sengoku/千石 branch is the one to verify' — the Sengoku branch closed in February 2023 per the Japanese GF closed-shop register, so the record redirects a celiac to a second shop that also no longer exists. Every citation defect here is repairable; the trading status is not. Mark closed or delist before anything else.

why: A chaffle is by definition a cheese-and-egg batter (「チーズや卵などを使って作る低糖質ワッフル」), and all five menu items carry cheese, egg, chicken or bacon. Tabelog's feature list says 「ベジタリアンメニューあり」 — vegetarian, never vegan, and the record's own vegan_detail concedes no confirmed plant-based item was found. 'Limited vegan options' overstates the evidence. Moot if the record is delisted as closed.
note: Downgrade recommendation, not an upgrade — recorded here for the human gate in REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md.

quote: Unverified establishment — no cross-contamination information could be sourced. Assume standard Japanese-kitchen wheat risks (wheat-based soy sauce/tsuyu, tempura batter, flour dusting, shared fryer) until confirmed in person.

Delete, or replace with a confirmed Kuramae venue such as アトミヨソワカ 蔵前 (vegan + gluten-free, 台東区蔵前4-17-4).

found: Menu page lists 「お野菜たっぷりプルコギ」 among the deli. But the shop's 「Vegetus+のこだわり」 page names only its seasonings 「塩はイタリア産の天然塩、砂糖はきび糖を使用しています。」 — soy sauce is never mentioned anywhere on the site.

quote: 国産雑穀米 multigrain rice may include barley (押し麦), a gluten grain — the base rice itself is a likely risk

quote: Shared deli case, serving utensils, and prep surfaces across all items; no dedicated gluten-free preparation
found: san-tatsu: 「ビュッフェのように自分でお皿に取り分けるスタイルもいいが、食べたいデリを注文し、店員さんが盛り付けてくれるため衛生面でも安心。」 — one open deli case, staff plating onto every plate. Tabelog: 12 seats, counter only.
note: Supported, and understated. The record omits the single biggest wheat vector on the premises — see the record_verdict row: the operator's own Tabelog PR says 「自家製ベーグルは専門店に負けない本格派！」, i.e. wheat bagels are baked in this 12-seat shop.

quote: Bulgogi and other soy-seasoned deli sides likely use wheat-containing soy sauce; no gluten-free tamari confirmed

note: Correctly hedged version of the same point. Cite the こだわり page — it is the page that would carry a tamari claim if one existed, and it does not.

found: こだわり page: 「保存料など不必要な添加物や化学調味料を使わずすべて手作りで作っています。」 Visit Chiyoda: 「保存料・化学調味料は使用されていません。」 Tabelog PR: 「化学調味料無添加でスープ、ドレッシング、ハムなどのシャルキュトリーも全て手作り！」

found: san-tatsu: 「オーナーの長谷川さん」 / 「長谷川さんの妻はイタリアへ料理留学し…現在は『vegetus+』を切り盛りをしている。」 Tabelog: 席数 12席, カウンター席あり, 貸切不可.

quote: Per the official Chiyoda city tourism listing, staff can identify which daily deli items are vegan and which are vegetarian
found: 「数あるメニューの中には、ベジタリアンやヴィーガン対応のものもあります。スタッフの方にその日はどれが対応メニューか聞くと丁寧にご紹介していただけます。」 — plus the page's own strict definition: 「「ヴィーガン」とは原材料に肉・魚介類・卵・乳製品・蜂蜜など動物由来の材料が使用されていないこととします。」
note: The claim names its source in prose but carries no URL — the rarest good kind of uncited claim, because the attribution is exactly right. Visit Chiyoda is the official 千代田区観光協会 site and says precisely this, under a definition of ヴィーガン that excludes honey. Attach the URL; no rewording needed.

quote: Deli/roast/salad style food means little deep-frying, lowering batter and shared-fryer gluten risk
found: Menu page: all eleven listed deli are roasts, marinades, salads and an omelette (低温ロースト, ハーブマリネ, スパイスロースト, キヌアサラダ…); no fried item appears anywhere on the menu.
note: Supported by the absence of any fried dish on the live menu. But 'lowering gluten risk' overall is now wrong on this record — the in-house bagel bakery is a bigger wheat vector than a fryer would be. See record_verdict.

quote: record-level assessment: gf_confidence=ask, vegan_status=options, trading
found: Operator's own Tabelog PR: 「化学調味料無添加でスープ、ドレッシング、ハムなどのシャルキュトリーも全て手作り！…自家製ベーグルは専門店に負けない本格派！」
method: record sweep — site subpages + Tabelog + Visit Chiyoda + san-tatsu interview
note: TRADING — open (Ameba Owned site © 2026, Visit Chiyoda listing live, no 掲載保留 or 閉店 flag on Tabelog, 2024 san-tatsu feature). Both tiers are correct: vegan_status 'options' is right (vegan-capable deli exist and staff will name them, but the case is mostly meat and fish and two of four dressings are dairy), and gf_confidence 'ask' is right. Every claim is real and merely needs its URL attached — EXCEPT for a serious omission: the shop bakes its own bagels (自家製ベーグル) and cures its own charcuterie in a 12-seat kitchen. Wheat flour is worked on these premises daily and the gf_cross_contamination field does not say so, while it does warn about hypothetical soy sauce. Add the bagel bakery as the primary wheat vector. Separately, the record's cuisine string reads 「有機野菜・ベジタリアン・グルテンフリー対応」 — no source anywhere (site, Tabelog, Gnavi, Visit Chiyoda, san-tatsu) uses the words グルテンフリー about this shop; drop that from the cuisine label.

quote: Wheat ramen noodles are the main product — flour/gluten is everywhere in the kitchen
found: Tabelog menu (updated 2026/01/03): 「鰹出汁の昆布水に合うように特注した喉越しの良い国産小麦の麺。…別添えの抹茶塩で麺だけを食べて頂き小麦の風味をお楽しみください。」
note: The shop's own menu says 国産小麦の麺 and invites you to enjoy 小麦の風味. Unambiguous. NOTE the citation must be the Ginza main store — see record_verdict, this record is pinned in the wrong part of Tokyo.

quote: Wheat-containing soy-sauce (shoyu) tare in every bowl

note: Shoyu kaeshi is named on the menu and on the shop's Takumen page. One caveat on the wording: 蛤SOBA and 蛤と帆立SOBA are built on 「特製の塩かえし」, so 'in every bowl' is slightly too broad — 'in the shoyu bowls, and no GF alternative anywhere' is the accurate form. 白醤油 is if anything more wheat-heavy than dark shoyu.

found: Tabelog listing: 予約不可, 4,635 reviews, 12,416 photos; reviewer 「外並びが既に出来てましたので、10分程待ってから券売機へ」. No allergen page exists on any of the shop's properties.

quote: record-level assessment: gf_confidence=no, vegan_status=no, WRONG LOCATION + WRONG CATEGORY
found: The cited Instagram account is 「むぎとオリ-ブ銀座本店」. Tabelog address: 東京都中央区銀座6-12-12 銀座ステラビル1F. The chain's branches are 銀座本店, 神田万世橋, 日本橋 and Narita T2 — no 根津 or 千駄木 branch exists in any source. The record's pin is lat 35.722 / lng 139.766 with neighborhood 「根津・千駄木（千駄木駅徒歩4分）」.
method: record sweep — Tabelog listing + menu, Takumen shop page, Yahoo Japan branch search
note: The safety claims are all true and all sourceable; the RECORD is wrong. (1) LOCATION: the pin sits in Nezu/Sendagi, roughly 6 km from the actual Ginza shop, and cites the Ginza branch's Instagram as if it were the local one — the brief's sibling-branch pattern, made worse by there being no sibling there at all. (2) CATEGORY: the record is filed as category BOTH with cuisine 「ヴィーガンベーカリー・グルテンフリー」 while carrying gf_confidence 'no' and vegan_status 'no'. A wheat-noodle, clam-and-chicken-stock ramen counter is being presented as a vegan gluten-free bakery. Fix the coordinates to the Ginza main store or drop the record; the cuisine string is simply false.
